ny-county-governing-body.area: New York State outside New York City
ny-county-governing-body.summary: In most of the state the County card names nobody. Three counties are answered; in the other 54 outside the city the card tells you which county you are in and not who governs it.
ny-county-governing-body.why: New York publishes no statewide list of county legislators or supervisors, so the only route is each county's own site, one at a time, and fourteen of the 57 would not answer this project at all.
ny-county-governing-body.wanted: Each county's own published list of the legislators or supervisors sitting today, and its district map where it elects by district.

ny-local-governing-body.concept: City, town or village governing body
ny-local-governing-body.area: New York State outside New York City
ny-local-governing-body.summary: Outside New York City the City or Town card names nobody. It tells you which city, town or village you are in, and not who sits on its board or council.
ny-local-governing-body.why: No statewide list of local board members is published, so the route is each government's own site. Of the hundred largest, two thirds served a page and about half of those link a board.
ny-local-governing-body.wanted: Each city, town and village's own published list of the members of its board or council, and its ward or district map where it elects by district.

ny-special-districts.area: New York State outside New York City
ny-special-districts.summary: No card names the fire, library, water or sewer district you are in. New York creates these by statute and some of them elect their own boards.
ny-special-districts.why: The state publishes no map of them. One county publishes its own full set and nothing has been found that covers the rest, so there is not yet a layer to switch on.
ny-special-districts.wanted: A county's own published map of its fire, library and other statutory districts, and whoever that county names as their officers.

ny-statewide-election-districts.area: New York State outside New York City
ny-statewide-election-districts.summary: Election districts are drawn for New York City only. Outside the city this layer does not answer.
ny-statewide-election-districts.why: The state does publish a statewide layer, and it is a year behind at least one county's own and too slow to open. The city's own source is current, so it is the one that ships.
ny-statewide-election-districts.wanted: A current statewide election-district layer, or a county's own published election districts for anywhere outside New York City.

ny-tribal-government.area: New York State outside New York City
ny-tribal-government.summary: No card names the tribal nation whose land you clicked on, or its government. Eight reservations lie upstate and two more sit on Long Island; the statewide cards answer at all of them and not one of them mentions the nation.
ny-tribal-government.why: Each nation publishes its own council, and its own election districts where it elects by district, on its own site. No state or federal source lists them together, so this app has no roster it could name anyone from.
ny-tribal-government.wanted: Each nation's own published list of its council members, and its district map where it elects by district.

nyc-amenity-phones.summary: Library cards carry no phone number.
nyc-amenity-phones.why: Neither of the two publishers this layer reads has a phone number in it — it's missing at the source, not undisplayed.
nyc-amenity-phones.wanted: A public-library dataset for New York — either the city's three systems or the state's — that includes branch phone numbers.

nyc-bronx-county-clerk.summary: The Bronx card names a County Clerk, and the city's own staff directory names somebody else for that seat. Every other borough is named and uncontested.
nyc-bronx-county-clerk.why: Two government publishers give different names, and the court system's site — the one the card's name came from — now turns this project away, so nothing we can read says which of the two is current.
nyc-bronx-county-clerk.wanted: Anything that settles who holds the Bronx County Clerk's office today: the office itself confirming it, or a dated notice of the appointment.

nyc-community-education-councils.summary: The Community Education Council card names your council and district but no members.
nyc-community-education-councils.why: Each council publishes its own members on its own site, and there is no single list covering all thirty-two, so this app has nothing it can read for every district.
nyc-community-education-councils.wanted: One list of Community Education Council members covering all thirty-two districts, or the thirty-two council sites named in one place so each can be read.

nyc-school-zone-details.summary: School-zone cards name the zoned school but carry no school address or grade range.
nyc-school-zone-details.why: The city's school zone data carries neither the school's address nor its grade range, so there is nothing to display.
nyc-school-zone-details.wanted: A DOE dataset joining zone to school address and grade span by DBN, refreshed each school year.
